Thanks for the time today - great discussion. Quick recap and next steps from our side:

- Goal: evaluate model fit for CuraHealth triage workflows (medical FAQ, scheduling, sensitive PHI redaction).
- Recommended initial models to benchmark:
  1) redwood-rlhf-13b - baseline for quality and instruction-following
  2) redwood-safety-7b - safety-tuned variant for refusal behavior
  3) redwood-quant-13b-q4 - latency/cost option for production

Attachments: model-eval-summary.pdf (high-level plan), prompt-sets.csv (curated prompts), benchmark-links.txt (scripts + datasets)

1) Can you confirm the sample size (~500 queries) and whether you can provide a redacted data dump (or synthetic data) for the initial run?
2) Any regulatory constraints we should know (state residency, data retention, audit windows)?
3) Who on your side will own the security questionnaire & evidence requests?

Safety note: we'll include a refusal/guardrail prompt set to stress-test sensitive domains (self-harm, PHI, drug prescriptions). Example guardrail snippet (included in attachments): "If the user requests medical advice or personal diagnoses, respond with a refusal and recommend seeking a licensed clinician. Offer to connect them to our scheduling flow."

Proposed next steps:
- We'll kick off benchmark runs once we have the sample data and a signed SOW/NDA - estimate 48-72 hours for the initial pass.
- Schedule a 60-minute results review: Thu, 18 Jun 2026 10:00 AM PT - are you available?

Great questions - answered inline below.

- Delta between models: redwood-rlhf-13b will generally give higher helpfulness and instruction adherence; redwood-safety-7b has targeted refusals and safer defaults but may be slightly more conservative on borderline clinical guidance. For patient-facing triage I usually recommend starting with both in parallel to quantify the tradeoffs on your prompts; we'll provide side-by-side metrics (helpfulness, hallucination rate, refusal rate).

- Quality regressions: we recommend a small labeled evaluation set (50-100 critical prompts) tracked across model versions. Redwood Optimize will run continuous evals and trigger alerts when token-level or intent-level metrics drift beyond thresholds. We'll also produce a per-prompt regression report and allow canary rollouts so you can route a small percentage to the new model.

- PII during evaluation: by default evaluation runs use ephemeral KV cache and request-level logs are redacted; raw identifiers are not stored persistently unless you opt into longer retention for troubleshooting. We can accept a redacted dump or synthetic dataset - synthetic is preferable for PHI-sensitive items. Neha is cc'd to provide the SOC2/KMS/audit details and confirm evidence we can share.

Timeline: once we have data + signed SOW/NDA, initial benchmark pass ~48-72 hours. We'll default to the 500-query size unless you request a different split.

Proposed kickoff: Thu, 18 Jun 2026 10:00 AM PT - I've tentatively booked that slot; please confirm.

Thanks,
Marissa

Hi all - Neha from Security & Compliance here. Quick summary / answers and attached evidence.

- PII handling: evaluation runs default to no persistent logging of raw identifiers. Request payloads are processed in-memory and only redacted summaries are retained in audit logs. We recommend you provide a redacted or synthetic dataset for the initial benchmark. If you require debugging with raw values, we can enable a short retention window under a specific support engagement.

- Guardrails & refusal testing: we maintain a prompt library and test harness that targets sensitive domains (PHI, self-harm, substance guidance). Example refusal template we recommend shipping to your product:
\  "Im sorry - I cant provide medical diagnoses or personalized medical advice. If you need urgent care, please call emergency services or contact your clinician. I can help schedule an appointment or provide general information."

- Safety eval artifacts: attached is safety-evals-summary.pdf and a guardrails-prompt-library.txt with curated prompts and expected responses (refuse/redirect patterns). We run these tests across model variants and include per-prompt pass/fail, false-accept rates, and a severity score.

- Evidence: SOC2 Type II summary, KMS/HSM encryption notes, and our audit-log retention policy are available - happy to provide full artifacts under the NDA.

I'll also share a short checklist you can hand to your procurement team describing what to expect during the security review.

Regards,
